# Windows Gotchas

> Known Windows OS administration patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Windows disk-full remediation gotchas (Installer orphans, read-only deletes, DISM, OneDrive sizing)](disk-full-remediation.md): C:\Windows\Installer orphan cleanup needs an all-orphan guard; read-only attribute silently blocks deletes; DISM no-ops with 0x800f080a until reboot; OneDrive placeholders inflate size reports past disk capacity. HIGH.
- [Dell SupportAssist SARemediation snapshots + unbounded VSS silently fill C:](dell-supportassist-snapshot-bloat.md): SupportAssist's SARemediation system-repair snapshots never self-prune (30+ GB, 2+ yrs deep) and pair with unbounded VSS; clearing once isn't enough, you must cap VSS and disable the "Dell SupportAssist Remediation" service. HIGH.
- [C:\Windows\Installer orphan detection: MSI COM returns 0 as SYSTEM, use the registry](installer-orphan-detection-registry.md): The WindowsInstaller COM ProductsEx/PatchesEx enumeration silently returns 0 products under the SYSTEM account (scheduled task), flagging every msi/msp orphaned; read LocalPackage from HKLM\...\Installer\UserData instead, with an all-orphan guard. Adobe Acrobat Reader's hoarded ~680MB .msp patches are the recurring cause. HIGH.
- [Runaway dllhost (DeviceMetadataRetrievalClient) pegs a CPU core; disable DsmSvc](device-metadata-dllhost-cpu-spin.md): A dllhost hosting COM {6C752774-...} (MetadataPackageSource) spins at 100% of one core with a tiny working set; PreventDeviceMetadataFromNetwork=1 + disabling the Metadata Refresh task won't stop the live loop (DsmSvc respawns it in ~25s, policy needs a reboot) — the no-reboot fix is to stop + disable DsmSvc. HIGH.
- [Low-disk triage order: Dell SA snapshots are NOT always the cause, even on Dell hardware](low-disk-triage-order.md): Don't assume Dell SupportAssist snapshots on a Dell; size C:\Windows\Temp and C:\Windows\Installer first. A Dell Latitude had SA at 0.27 GB but Temp at 12.2 GB, and a Surface had 50 GB Installer (20 GB orphaned). SAFE-tier cleanup often clears the alert without touching any vendor store. MEDIUM.
- [PrintService Event 600 / 800702e4 is elevation-required, not a bad driver -- non-WHQL Point-and-Print drivers need the publisher cert in TrustedPublisher](pointprint-nonwhql-driver-trust.md): Non-admins get a repeating "trust this printer / install driver" prompt and Event 600 error 800702e4 (= ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED, misleadingly blamed on the driver/signature) when a print server serves a newer, vendor-signed (non-WHQL) driver under the PrintNightmare mitigation; fix = add the vendor publisher cert to TrustedPublisher, never disable RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators. HIGH.
- [printui /ga hangs forever in session 0 when the shared printer's driver is not pre-installed](printui-ga-session0-driver-hang.md): The per-machine connection add waits on an invisible Point-and-Print trust dialog (no error, no event, no registry entry); pre-stage the driver from the print server's DriverStore via pnputil + Add-PrinterDriver, then /ga returns instantly, and restart the spooler to surface the connection. HIGH.
- [Fake-antivirus toasts "via Microsoft Edge" are web push, not malware -- and the cleanup has four traps](edge-push-notification-scareware-cleanup.md): "Your PC is infected with N viruses" popups plus Windows toasts are Edge web-push from an accidentally-Allowed origin, not an infection (if the popup says McAfee and the box only has Defender, it is fake by definition); the cleanup fails silently because Edge rewrites Preferences on exit, runs windowless under --no-startup-window, MainWindowHandle is always 0 from SYSTEM, and the Windows-side per-origin AUMID sender must be removed separately. HIGH.
- [A replacement PC's synced browser profile carries history but NOT site permissions](synced-browser-profile-permissions-not-synced.md): Chromium sync ships history/passwords/extensions but deliberately excludes content_settings, so a fresh profile on a swapped laptop shows weeks of synced history alongside 0 notification grants — and the zero describes only the NEW device. A 3h-old Edge profile held 12,793 visits and 0 grants while the scareware grant sat on the powered-off old laptop. Split conclusions by datatype: history is cross-device evidence, permissions/toast senders are per-device and stay OUTSTANDING. HIGH.
- [An aggressive battery sleep timeout makes a laptop effectively unmanageable, and reads as a flaky agent](aggressive-battery-sleep-unmanageable.md): standby-timeout-dc of 0xb4 (180 s) drops an in-use laptop off the network every 3 idle minutes, so RMM agents appear to flap and you chase the agent instead of the power policy; pin timeouts for the maintenance window, and always restore LIDACTION (0 = do nothing will cook the machine in a bag) verifying via registry because powercfg /query returns nothing for it. MEDIUM.
